Signalith security report for siem-1
Checked 2026-10-13 14:02 UTC. Signalith v0.9.0 (go1.26.10). Linux, systemd
service.

Summary: 1 at risk, 3 need attention, 15 good, 2 Signalith can't check from
here.

Fix first
1. At risk: Connection to OpenSearch
   Signalith doesn't check OpenSearch's certificate, so someone on the network
   could pose as OpenSearch and read events and its password.
   How to fix:
   - Set CA certificate file to the certificate of the authority that signed
     OpenSearch's.
   - Then turn off Skip certificate check, and restart when asked.
   Setting: opensearch.tls_skip_verify (Settings page, OpenSearch)
   Docs: https://github.com/jrsamsanchez/signalith/blob/v0.9.0/docs/opensearch-security.md#4-point-signalith-at-it
2. Needs attention: Built-in admin's password
   The built-in admin still has the first password the Docker setup made,
   which is kept as plain text in a Docker volume.
   How to fix:
   - Set a password of its own for the built-in admin, then restart Signalith.
   Run:
     sudo signalith passwd && sudo systemctl restart signalith
   Docs: https://github.com/jrsamsanchez/signalith/blob/v0.9.0/docs/users.md#the-built-in-admin
3. Needs attention: Certificate authority
   A new certificate authority is ready. Switch to it once browsers and agents
   trust it.
   How to fix:
   - Continue under Switching certificate authority, at the top of the
     Security page.
   Docs: https://github.com/jrsamsanchez/signalith/blob/v0.9.0/docs/https.md#switching-to-a-new-certificate-authority
4. Needs attention: Syslog
   Syslog over UDP is accepted from any computer that can reach port 514, so
   anyone could send fake events.
   In the last day: 4 devices over UDP.
   How to fix:
   - List the addresses or ranges of the devices that send syslog, such as
     10.0.0.0/8.
   Setting: syslog.allow (Settings page, Syslog)
   Docs: https://github.com/jrsamsanchez/signalith/blob/v0.9.0/docs/security.md#syslog

In transit
  [at risk]     Connection to OpenSearch
                Signalith doesn't check OpenSearch's certificate, so someone
                on the network could pose as OpenSearch and read events and
                its password.
  [attention]   Certificate authority
                A new certificate authority is ready. Switch to it once
                browsers and agents trust it.
  [attention]   Syslog
                Syslog over UDP is accepted from any computer that can reach
                port 514, so anyone could send fake events.
  [good]        HTTPS
                The web page, the API and agents use HTTPS, with Signalith's
                own certificate.
  [good]        Agents on plain HTTP
                Agents can only send events over HTTPS.
  [good]        HTTPS certificate
                Signalith's own certificate is valid until 2027-08-09 and
                renews itself 30 days before.
  [good]        Agent port
                Agents send to a port of their own (7779), and the web port
                turns them away.

At rest
  [can't tell]  Disk encryption
                Signalith's files are on a virtual disk. Its host (Amazon EC2)
                may encrypt it, but Signalith can't see that from inside.
                How to check:
                - Check the disk's settings in Amazon EC2's console, or ask
                  whoever runs the host.
                Docs: https://github.com/jrsamsanchez/signalith/blob/v0.9.0/docs/security.md#disk-encryption
  [can't tell]  Where OpenSearch keeps events
                OpenSearch runs on another computer (10.0.0.20), so Signalith
                can't see its disk.
                How to check:
                - On the computer OpenSearch runs on, check the disk that
                  holds its data folder (path.data in opensearch.yml).
                Run:
                  lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS
                Docs: https://github.com/jrsamsanchez/signalith/blob/v0.9.0/docs/security.md#where-opensearch-keeps-events
  [good]        Who can read OpenSearch
                OpenSearch turns away anyone who doesn't sign in.
  [good]        Master key
                The master key is in /var/lib/signalith/keys/master.key, and
                only signalith can read it.
                Make it stronger: Give the key to the service as a systemd
                credential, so it can live outside Signalith's folders.
  [good]        Stored passwords and keys
                The one stored password or key is encrypted with the master
                key.
                Signalith's HTTPS keys and the Docker setup's generated
                secrets are protected by file permissions, not by the master
                key (see File permissions).

In use
  [good]        Memory
                Signalith's memory can't be saved in a crash dump, and other
                programs can't read it, except as root.
                Swap: off for Signalith.
                Make it stronger: For more protection, run Signalith in a
                confidential virtual machine (AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX), which
                is built to keep even its host from reading its memory.

Accounts and sign-in
  [attention]   Built-in admin's password
                The built-in admin still has the first password the Docker
                setup made, which is kept as plain text in a Docker volume.
  [good]        Two-step sign-in
                Admins who sign in with a password also enter a code from an
                authenticator app.
                Other users can turn two-step sign-in on for themselves from
                the user menu.
  [good]        Signalith's OpenSearch account
                Signalith signs in to OpenSearch as signalith, an account
                without admin rights.
  [good]        Everyday sign-in
                Only the built-in admin signs in so far.
                Make it stronger: Give yourself an admin account on the Users
                page, then turn the built-in admin off and keep it for
                emergencies. The audit log then shows who did what.
  [good]        Sign-in sessions
                People are signed out after 1 hour without use, unless they
                choose Keep me signed in, and every sign-in ends after 1 day.

This server
  [good]        File permissions
                Signalith's keys and private files can only be read by its own
                account.
  [good]        Account Signalith runs as
                Signalith runs as its own account (signalith), not as root.
  [good]        Service protections
                Signalith's service runs with all the protections its systemd
                unit sets up.

Always on
  - Passwords, API sign-ins and sessions are refused over plain HTTP, and the
    sign-in cookie is sent over HTTPS only.
  - Browsers that reach Signalith by name are told to use HTTPS only (HSTS).
  - Every page has a strict Content Security Policy and can't be shown inside
    another site.
  - Guessing passwords is slowed: after 10 wrong tries for one account from
    one address in 15 minutes, sign-in pauses for 15 minutes. The API is
    limited the same way.
  - Sign-ins end after 24 hours by default (30 days at most), even with Keep
    me signed in.
  - Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes.
  - Logs, pages and the API never show stored passwords or keys.
  - Agents set up from Add data check the server's certificate before sending.
  - Sign-ins, sign-outs and every change to users and settings go to the audit
    log.

Not checked here
  - Firewalls: which computers can reach Signalith's ports.
  - Backups, and whether the master key is kept apart from them.
  - Updates for Signalith, OpenSearch and the operating system. Signalith
    doesn't contact the internet to check.
  - The computers agents run on.
  - Copies of events outside Signalith, such as exports, moved archives and
    OpenSearch snapshots.
  How to check these yourself:
  https://github.com/jrsamsanchez/signalith/blob/v0.9.0/docs/security.md#not-checked-here
